gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the REDTIGER F77 does have a microSD slot but cannot record to it: the card only copies files off the camera and loads firmware, so the 128 GB or 256 GB internal eMMC is all the recording space it will ever have. ChatGPT told the shopper the F77 has 'no SD card slot'.
standout_why: I tried to open the cited rival pages: 70mai.store M500, incartec M500, the DDPAI Z90 Master US page and shopredtiger.shop F77, plus the 70mai M800 manual on manuals.plus. Every one failed (HTTP 429, a certificate error, a DNS failure, or a PDF with no text layer), so I could not read their text directly. ChatGPT's answer, which was built from those pages, says the F77 has 'no SD card slot' and says nothing on what each slot does. A named reviewer (DT MI, DashCamTalk) states the slot exists, does not record, and takes cards up to 256 GB. The official 70mai M800 page states the RC14 rear camera comes only in the '4K M800 set'. Neither fact appears in ChatGPT's answer. The DDPAI microSD expansion is already in ChatGPT's answer ('optional microSD expansion'), so that part is not new.
decides: If the shopper wants built-in memory plus a way to add more, the only shown model that records to a card is the DDPAI Z90 Master: 64 GB eMMC plus microSD up to 512 GB, per DashCamTalk's data sheet. Dealectric's own DDPAI Z90 Pro and N5 Pro listings are also described as 64 GB eMMC + microSD. The F77, M800 and M500 all have fixed recording storage. The F77's slot only copies files and loads firmware. On the M800 the front and rear cameras share 128 GB, and the official page mentions no microSD. That favours the DDPAI line over ChatGPT's pick, the M800, for anyone who records long trips. For a 'set it and forget it' buyer, the F77 includes its hardwire kit, according to DashCamTalk's review. The 70mai M500 needs a hardwire kit sold separately for parking mode. The M800's rear camera comes only with the '4K M800 set', so a shopper who buys the front-only listing does not get front and rear.

findings.label: microSD slot role
findings.value: Slot present; cannot record to it; used to copy files and for firmware updates
findings.source_title: REDTIGER F77 Version 1 (128GB) Review and Impressions (DashCamTalk, reviewer DT MI, posted 2025-08-02)
findings.note: Quote: 'There is a slot for a micro SD card which can be used for copying files but you cannot record directly to it. It's also used for updating firmware.'

findings.label: microSD card size accepted (copy/firmware only)
findings.source_title: REDTIGER F77 Version 1 (128GB) Review and Impressions (DashCamTalk, DT MI)
findings.note: Quote: 'Cards of up to 256GB are supported.' This card size does not add recording space.

findings.label: Built-in recording storage
findings.value: 128 GB eMMC (a 256 GB version is also sold)
findings.source_title: REDTIGER F77 Version 1 (128GB) Review and Impressions (DashCamTalk, DT MI)

unsourced: DDPAI Z90 Master eMMC capacity: the DashCamTalk page gives both 64 GB and 32 GB. I tried ddpai.com/en-us/products/z90-master and ddpai.com/dash-cams/z90-series/; both returned HTTP 429. The manuals.plus manual returned 403.
How DDPAI splits footage between eMMC and microSD (which files go where): looked for it on the DDPAI pages (429) and on DashCamTalk, which does not say.
DDPAI Z90 Pro and N5 Pro microSD limits and hardwire kit model: the DDPAI site was rate-limited for the whole session.

Which 70mai hardwire kit model the M500 and M800 officially pair with (UP03/UP06 for parking, a 4G kit for the M800): 70mai.store/products/up03-hardwire-kit and 70mai.my returned 429. The official M500, M800, UP06 and UP05 pages name no models.
70mai M500 eMMC capacity variants: the official M500 page gives none; 70mai.store returned 429.

REDTIGER F77 maker page (storage variants, slot wording, kit contents): redtigercam.com returned 429, shopredtiger.shop did not resolve (DNS), the ezdashcam manual PDF returned 404, and the device.report manual returned 403.
70mai M800 manual (manuals.plus PDF): the PDF has no text layer and I could not extract it, so the M800's microSD and accessory statements come from the official page only.
US prices for every candidate: storecheck.py returned HTTP 429 for 70mai.store, ddpai.com and redtigercam.com. I did not try Amazon.
